rv.q: Hyland’s indie rock adaptation of the 1896. Russian play reaches for the emotional depth and artistic sensibility of “Rent” or “Once,” and although the writing is not on par with these celebrated musicals, it is sprinkled with sharply insightful lines and lyrics.
Despite its flaws, Seagulls crackles with an undeniable energy thanks to its game cast.
Some dramatic details also hamper the show’s effectiveness.

cn.t: This indie rock Chekhov adaptation set on a modern college campus shows promise with sharply insightful moments, but the writing doesn't quite reach the emotional depth it aspires to, leaving critics moderately impressed.
